Hi Sergio,

Thanks for sending over the draft US privacy addendum last week. Our legal team did a first pass and had a couple of clarifying questions before we route to procurement:

1) Subprocessor visibility — can Redwood provide a near-real-time inventory (or at least weekly export) of active subprocessors supporting our account? The current clause requiring notice "where feasible" is vague for us given our audit cadence.

2) Interstate transfer mapping — for the limited-use / processor scenario under CCPA/CPRA, we need a short mapping table that shows where telemetry/telemetry-backup and logs are stored geographically (state-level) and whether any onshore fallback exists. A simple CSV would work.

3) Evidence — we will need a SOC 2 cert and the dataflow diagram referenced in the DPA for our security review. If there are subprocessor contracts (or a summary), please include those as well.

Can you confirm what you can share and the approximate timeline? We are hoping to get this to our procurement review by Friday.

Best,
Emma

Hi all,

Thanks Emma — appreciate the specific asks. Proposed approach below (I included a redline attached to show the exact clause edits):

- Subprocessor visibility: We can provide a weekly CSV export that lists active subprocessors, purpose, and last-updated timestamp. For material changes (onboarding of a new subprocessor that processes personal information), we will provide push notice within 5 business days and, on request, deliver a copy of the applicable subprocessor agreement redacted for commercial terms.

- Transfer mapping (state-level): Attached is a short state mapping for telemetry and logs. We designate primary storage in us-west-2 (California) with onshore backups in us-east-1 (Virginia). Telemetry export endpoints are in CA and VA; encrypted at rest using customer-keyed KMS where enabled. We will produce a one-page CSV mapping for your procurement team.

- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II report (summary) is shareable under NDA. We also have a personnel access control diagram and the referenced dataflow diagram — links below.

Suggested narrow redline to the addendum: replace "where feasible" notice language with: \"Redwood will provide a weekly export of active subprocessors for the customer account and shall, within five (5) business days of onboarding any new subprocessor that will process Customer Personal Information, notify Customer and provide a redacted copy of the subprocessor agreement upon request.\"

Attachments: subprocessor_inventory_Q2_2026.xlsx, redline_uspa_draft.docx

If that works, Ben — can you confirm we'll be willing to accept the redaction-only share of agreements and that Sales will commit to the weekly export operationally? Emma — if acceptable, I'll send the SOC2 summary under an NDA link later today.

1) Timing — 5 business days for material onboarding is acceptable; can you add a "for critical subprocessors (security or auth providers) we will provide 48-hour pre-notice when onboarding to avoid service interruptions" carve-out?

3) SOC2 — we can sign a short mutual NDA if required; otherwise please provide the SOC2 summary link. Also requesting the dataflow diagram shared link for internal review.

If you can confirm those three points, we'll move the addendum to procurement review. Appreciate the quick turnaround.
